findings.explanation: The SPL only keeps events whose provider equals `microsoft-windows-search`. As I recall, the Application events 7040 and 7042 about a corrupt catalog are shown with Source 'Windows Search Service', while Microsoft-Windows-Search is the provider for the 1xxx-series events. If the XML provider name differs, the search silently returns nothing. The negative test even uses a Microsoft-Windows-Search ID 1004 event.
findings.quote: Windows Application XML from the Microsoft Windows Search provider, Event IDs 7040 and 7042
findings.suggested_fix: On a real or lab Windows build, open a 7040 or 7042 event in Event Viewer (Details > XML) and record the exact Provider Name. Then set the provider predicate (and the controlTest fixtures) to that value, or accept both names.

findings.explanation: UC-1.2.19 gives the same XmlWinEventLog source contract as 'version 6.0.0+', and the Windows guide lists 'current' as 9.0+. This UC (and splunkbaseApps minVersion) requires exactly 10.0.1. Check on Splunkbase that 10.0.1 exists, and whether the XML source types really need that release rather than 6.0.0.
findings.quote: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (`Splunk_TA_windows`, Splunkbase 742), version 10.0.1.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm the add-on version history for 742 and use one minimum version consistently across the 1.2.x UCs, for example '6.0.0 or later'.

findings.explanation: The SPL returns one row per event and has no count, so 'repeated 7040' is not detectable. The dashboard's repeat-count table by endpoint needs a separate search.
findings.quote: notify the endpoint owner on any 7042 or repeated 7040
findings.suggested_fix: Define 'repeated' (for example, 3 events in 24 hours) and add the aggregation to a companion search, or drop the wording.

findings.explanation: The URL is a Microsoft Q&A community question (learn.microsoft.com/answers/questions/...), not a Microsoft Support article, so the title overstates its authority.
findings.quote: "title": "Microsoft Support example: Search Event IDs 7040 and 7042 catalog-corruption messages"
findings.suggested_fix: Retitle it as a community Q&A example, and prefer a documentation page for the event text.

findings.explanation: This text answers a boilerplate statement that is not in this UC. It is authoring residue and will confuse readers.
findings.quote: no invented 300-900 second vendor interval applies
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the sentence and describe only how Application events are collected.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The hard-coded `event_provider="microsoft-windows-search"` filter should be confirmed against the real provider name of Application events 7040 and 7042 (see dataSources finding). A wrong name would produce zero rows with no error.
The array holds a prose 'N/A (...)' string rather than technique IDs or an empty list.

summary: A well-scoped fault detection with honest limits. The main risks are an unverified provider name that the SPL hard-codes and an add-on version that disagrees with sibling UCs. The repeat-count wording is not backed by the SPL.
